title: Groovy Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: println prints a value with a newline.

examples.title: Name a value
examples.description: def declares a variable without spelling its type.

examples.title: Build a message
examples.description: Double-quoted strings can place a variable in the text with a dollar sign.

examples.title: Choose an action
examples.description: if selects a block based on a rule.
examples.code:
def score = 8
if (score >= 5) { println "Pass" } else { println "Try again" }

examples.title: Read a list item
examples.description: A list stores ordered values. Its first position is zero.

examples.title: Read a named field
examples.description: A map pairs keys with values. Dot syntax can read a simple text key.
examples.code:
def book = [title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24]
println book.title

examples.title: Count across a range
examples.description: The range 1..3 includes both endpoints. each visits the values.

examples.title: Name a small function
examples.description: A closure is a block of reusable code. The arrow separates inputs from steps.
examples.code:
def twice = { n -> n * 2 }
println twice(4)

examples.title: Transform each item
examples.description: collect builds a list from a closure result for each item.

examples.title: Keep matching items
examples.description: findAll keeps items for which the closure result is true.

examples.title: Handle a missing object
examples.description: ?. skips a property read on null. The Elvis operator ?: supplies a fallback for a false-like value.

examples.title: Create an object
examples.description: A class groups data fields and actions. Groovy supports named property values during construction.
